implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.TicTacToeGame.__init__ creates self.board as a 3x3 list of lists; gui._setup_ui creates a 3x3 grid of tk.Buttons.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate turns with marks X and O
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.current_player initialized to 'X' and switched in switch_player(); gui updates status with game.get_current_player().
game_logic.move_history records (player_mark, row, col) on every successful make_move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate moves (inside board and on empty cells)
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.is_valid_move checks bounds and that the cell contains a space.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Determine the winner when a player gets three in a row
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic._find_winning_line scans rows, columns, and diagonals; make_move sets self.winner and self.winning_line when a line is found.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when the board is full with no winner
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.is_board_full and make_move set self.game_over when the board is full and no winner; is_draw returns True in that case.

implemented_requirements.requirement: User‑friendly graphical interface with clickable cells
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.TicTacToeGUI builds a Tkinter window with a 3x3 button grid; each button calls _on_cell_click to apply a move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Display current player turn and game result
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui._update_status shows "Player X's turn"; _handle_game_end shows win/draw message via status label and messagebox.
gui._highlight_winning_line changes background of the three winning cells using game.winning_line.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Provide a way to start a new game
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui includes a "New Game" button that calls _reset_game, which resets the logic and UI.

judge.summary: All core requirements for a two‑player Tic‑Tac‑Toe game are fully implemented. The logic module handles board state, move validation, turn alternation, win/draw detection, and move history. The Tkinter GUI presents a clear 3x3 clickable grid, shows turn information, announces results, highlights the winning line, and offers a New Game button. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to run, giving a high likelihood of successful execution.
